stem.en: An object is moving with a constant velocity. Is a net force acting on it?

text.en: No. The net force on it is zero.

feedback.en: Right. Its velocity does not change, so by the first law the net force is zero.

text.en: Yes. A net force is needed to keep it moving.

feedback.en: No force is needed to keep an object moving at a constant velocity. A net force would change its velocity.

text.en: Yes. A net force equal to its weight acts on it.

feedback.en: The weight is balanced by the push of the floor. The net force on the object is zero.

explanation.en: Constant velocity means zero acceleration. By Newton's first law, the net force on the object is zero.

hints.en: Does the velocity of the object change?
